scenes.tts: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January. Yet January is winter in the north. So distance does not make the seasons. Earth's axis is tilted about twenty three point four degrees. Through the year, each hemisphere in turn leans toward the Sun, and gets more direct light and longer days.

scenes.tts: Shine a torch straight down at a table and you get a small bright spot. Tilt it, and the same light covers more ground. At the top of the atmosphere, a surface facing the Sun gets about one thousand three hundred sixty watts. That is per square metre. Put the Sun sixty degrees from overhead, and a flat surface gets half of that.

scenes.tts: Now spread that light over the whole planet. Earth intercepts sunlight on a disk. But it spreads that light over a sphere. A sphere has four times the area of the disk. So the global mean at the top of the atmosphere is one thousand three hundred sixty divided by four. That is three hundred forty watts per square metre. Averaged over a year, the tropics get more, and the poles get less.

scenes.tts: That uneven heating moves the air. Near the equator, warm moist air rises. As it rises it cools, its water vapour condenses, and it rains. The dry air flows poleward at height and sinks in the subtropics. Sinking air is compressed and warms, so rain is suppressed. The Sahara and the Kalahari lie under this sinking air. This loop is the Hadley cell, an idealized model.

scenes.tts: A Walter Lieth diagram puts monthly temperature and rainfall on one chart, with ten degrees level with twenty millimetres. Take a made up lowland station at twenty six degrees all year. That temperature plots at fifty two millimetres. Its driest month, September, has ninety millimetres, above that line, so there is no dry period. The Koppen Geiger rules call it A f, a tropical rainforest climate.
scenes.caption: A Walter-Lieth diagram puts monthly temperature and rainfall on one chart, with 10 degrees level with 20 millimetres. Take a made-up lowland station at 26 degrees all year. That temperature plots at 52 millimetres. Its driest month, September, has 90 millimetres, above that line, so there is no dry period. The Köppen-Geiger rules call it Af, a tropical rainforest climate.

scenes.tts: That match is a hypothesis to test against the vegetation actually present. Staver and colleagues analysed tree cover across the tropics of Africa, Australia and South America. Take yearly rain between about one thousand and twenty five hundred millimetres, with a dry season under seven months. There, places were mostly savanna or forest. Fire was associated with keeping areas open. Savanna and forest may be alternative states under the same climate. Climate predicts a biome roughly. It does not fix it.
